title: Screen Watcher
description: Local desktop application that detects visual changes and builds a semantic history of screen activity.

title: TinyDB
description: Key-value database built from scratch to explore indexing, append-only storage and log compaction through benchmarks.

title: Kafka Market Stream
description: Real-time market data pipeline that streams Binance trades through Kafka to independent consumers and a live dashboard.

title: Unity vs Unreal Face AR
description: One-day experiment comparing Unity and Unreal Engine by building the same Android face-tracking AR experience.

title: Local Academic RAG
description: Local RAG system with structure-aware retrieval, grounded generation and traceable sources over academic documents.

title: Adaptive Edge-Cloud Inference
description: Adaptive vision system where global Cloud detections guide local Edge attention, reducing remote inference calls by 71% and transferred data by 74% in a reproducible video benchmark.

title: Personal Web Search
description: From-scratch web search engine with controlled crawling, an inverted index and BM25 ranking, revisiting a personal search engine project from 2022.

title: GLB Stress Lab
description: Browser performance experiment comparing main-thread and Web Worker GLB loading, measuring responsiveness, blocking time and time to first rendered frame across increasingly large 3D assets.

title: Desktop Dragon
description: Persistent Windows desktop pet with global eye tracking, direct interaction and a lightweight Tamagotchi-style state that continues evolving while the application is closed.

title: Portfolio 2026
description: Personal portfolio built as Stage I of the 30 Projects challenge, combining selected engineering case studies with a README-driven challenge tracker that updates as new projects are released.

title: Cellular Radar for AOSP
description: Native Android 17 Settings extension for inspecting framework-reported cellular information, including serving and observed cells, network identity, radio technology, frequency and signal metrics. Built directly into AOSP and validated on Cuttlefish.

title: Agentic Visual QA
description: Autonomous black-box web QA system combining deterministic browser checks, LLM-driven semantic exploration and VLM screenshot perception, with validated execution, replay and evidence-based defect reporting.

title: CUDA Vision Bench
description: Custom CUDA Gaussian Blur benchmark comparing naive and shared-memory tiled kernels against OpenCV CPU and OpenCV CUDA. Separates kernel-only from end-to-end performance to expose the impact of GPU memory transfers.

title: Crypto Strength Bench
description: Visual cryptography benchmark measuring real CPU and RTX 3090 CUDA SHA-256 throughput, then extrapolating exhaustive-search times across increasingly large key spaces. Includes matched CPU/GPU comparison, PBKDF2 and controlled synthetic secret recovery.

title: RING — FPGA vs STM32
description: Hardware-in-the-loop Pong experiment comparing FPGA and STM32 controllers under the same Windows-hosted physics and serial protocol. Implements a quantized neural-network policy in SystemVerilog on an Arty A7-35T and a FreeRTOS controller on STM32, with real-time dual-UART telemetry and physical hardware execution.

title: PUSHLESS
description: Experimental Android benchmark exploring how far self-hosted push notifications can work without Firebase or another push provider. Compares WebSocket, MQTT, periodic polling and foreground-service delivery across background, screen-off, Doze, network-loss and process-death conditions on a physical Android device.

title: Quant Ladder
description: Quantization benchmark mapping the speed, efficiency and quality trade-off of Qwen3-8B from F16 down to Q2_K on an RTX 3090. Measures throughput, VRAM, energy, perplexity, KL divergence and GSM8K accuracy, identifying Q4_K_M as the compression knee.

title: Pocket LLama
description: On-device LLM experiment measuring how large a model a physical Android phone can run before it stops being interactive. Runs Qwen3 0.6B–8B (Q4_K_M) through llama.cpp via NDK/JNI on a Galaxy Z Fold6 CPU, fully offline, recording load time, prefill/decode throughput, memory and thermal throttling to separate fits, usable and interactive.

title: Voice Ladder
description: Local zero-shot voice-cloning benchmark measuring how much reference audio a cloner needs to sound like the speaker. Climbs a 3 s → 5 min reference ladder for XTTS-v2, Chatterbox Multilingual and F5-TTS (Spanish) on an RTX 3090 using Multilingual LibriSpeech readers, scoring ECAPA speaker similarity, Whisper ΔWER, DNSMOS, RTF and VRAM. Finds that raw audio plateaus after ~10 s, while picking the best 10 s window from 5 min lifts similarity to 0.775 (ceiling 0.904).
